title: Best Road Trip Snacks for Kids in NZ — No-Mess, No-Meltdown Options
meta_desc: Discover the best no-mess road trip snacks for kids in NZ, with prices from $2-$5
intro: Long road trips with kids can be challenging, especially when it comes to snacks. A well-stocked snack bag can make all the difference between a harmonious drive and a meltdown. With drive times between Auckland and Queenstown ranging from 18-20 hours, it's essential to have a plan in place.

sections.heading: Practical Snack Ideas for Long Drives
sections.body: When choosing snacks for a road trip, consider options that are easy to eat, won't make a mess, and can withstand temperature changes. Some excellent choices include fresh fruits like apples ($1.50 each at Countdown) and oranges ($2.00 each at New World), as well as energy-rich granola bars ($3.50 for a 6-pack at Pak'nSave).

sections.heading: Supermarket Options for Road Trip Snacks
list: New World's in-store bakery ($2-$5 per item)

sections.heading: Cooler Tips for Perishable Snacks
sections.body: A cooler is essential for keeping perishable snacks fresh during long drives. When packing a cooler, place ice packs at the bottom and top to maintain a consistent temperature. Some great cooler options include the ChillTech 25L Cooler ($49.99 at The Warehouse) and the Coleman 30L Cooler ($69.99 at Mitre 10).

Avoiding Meltdowns with Regular Breaks
sections.body: Regular breaks are crucial for preventing meltdowns during long drives. Aim to stop every 2-3 hours at rest stops or parks, such as the Hamilton Gardens (free admission) or the Taupo Hot Springs (adults $20, children $10). These breaks allow kids to stretch their legs, get some fresh air, and use the bathroom.
